MESO-SCALE (1:10,000) LANDSLIDE SUSCEPTIBILITY MAPPING IN PARTS OF
TIRUMALA HILLS, CHITTOOR DISTRICT, ANDHRA PRADESH
In pursuance of the field season pro gram 2022 -23, Meso-scale (1:10,000) landslide
susceptibility mapping was carried out in parts of Tirumala hills, Chittoor District, Andhra
Pradesh, vide Item Code- M4LSSI/NC/SR/2022/43764. The study area falls in SOI Toposheet
No. 57O/6 and bounded by coordinates 13°41'30.22"N 79°20'14.65"E and 13°38'23.06"N,
79°25'24.21"E.  The study was undertaken with the objectives of i). To identify slope -failure
domains and to prepare domain -specific geo -factor maps in a GIS. ii). To rate and weigh
relevant geo-factor maps for different failure domains iii). To integrate the rated and weighted
geo-factor maps per identified failure domain in a GIS iv). To combine the  domain-specific
landslide susceptibility models into a combined and classified landslide susceptibility map on
Geologically the Tirumala hill area is comprising Granitoids of Peninsular Gneiss ic
Complex (PGC) overlain by Bairenkonda Quartzites and Cumbum Shales and Schist Stones.
The PGC is later intruded by basic dykes.
During the course of fieldwork, landslide incidences were integrated with various
thematic maps like slope map, aspect map, LULC map,  Geomorphon map, geological slope
forming material map etc. and their distribution was analysed to bring out the final
susceptibility map of the entire study area.
The landslide susceptibility map was categorised into low, moderate and high
susceptibility zones by using the various thematic maps for rockslide, debris slide and cut slope
domain respectively. Landslide Susceptibility Estimated Rating (LSER) value and
consequently the weightage to the thematic maps have been assigned to all the classes and
features related to respective thematic maps. The assigned weightage is multiplied by the
respective thematic map and the value -added thematic map is divided by the total weightage
of the maps used to produce the final susceptibility score map using Arc -GIS software. The
whole process is integrated in a GIS using the Weighted Multi-class Index Overlay method and
these domains specified susceptibility maps are finally combined as a Combined Landslide
The ALOS PALSAR Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data (12.5m) have been used to
create the various thematic maps which include a base map, slope aspect, slope gradient,
relative relief, drainage, Stream Power Index (SPI), Landform (Geomorphon) and LULC maps
using software like Arc GIS 10.2.1, GRASS GIS 7.6 and Google Earth.
The causative factors for landslide occurrence were identified and mapped during the
field investigation.  These include the preparation of a domain -wise Slope Forming Map,
Kinematic failure map, Geo -technical map of rocks & ove rburden based on RMR rating and
cohesion value respectively, Landslide Inventory Map, and updating of land use land cover
map. A total of 48 nos. of landslide incidences were recorded during the fieldwork, out of
which 34 nos. are Debris slide, and 14 nos.  are Rockslide and Rock Fall. Almost all the
landslides were recorded from Tirumala up-road section, and majorly concentrated along cut-
slopes of the corridor. The study area has been classified into three susceptibility classes i.e.,
Low or No slide domain, moderate and highly susceptibility zone. Low or No slide domain is
occupying 40.08%, moderate susceptibility zone 43.59% and high susceptibility zone 12.33%
of 36.17 sq. km of the total area. The road corridor from Alipiri to Tirumala (Tirumala up-ghat
road), from chainage 0 km to 8 and 16 -18 km is under very low hazard and low risk category
while the road corridor from 9 km to 12 km are under moderate hazard and moderate risk
category and the road corridor from 13 to 16 are under high hazard and high-risk category.
Based on the computed hazard descriptor, rock mass quality and intensity of the
landslide, a generic hazard mitigation plan is prepared for Debris slide zones and Rockslide
zones.  The five hair pin bends of Tirumala up road from milestone 12km to 16km road corridor
is fall under highly susceptible zone. Some general mitigation options provided for debris slides
are removal of soil from the head of the slide, slope grading or benching of unstable slope,
Stream channel linings, check dams, reta ining walls, slope stabilization using vegetation and
debris hazard Warning Signs. The general rockfall hazard mitigation options provided for
vulnerable zones along Tirumala Up -Ghat Road include catch ditches, benches, scaling and
trimming, cable and mesh , shotcrete, anchors, rock bolts and Rock fall/Rockslide hazard

To mitigate the risk of landslides, it is essential to understand the factors that
contribute to them and take appropriate measures to prevent them. Mesoscale Landslide
Susceptibility Mapping being carried out on a large scale (1:10000) helps to show where and
how many chances of landslides occur in an area. The basic methodology is to prepare
thematic maps of the causative factors of slope and to establish the susceptibility level by
layering them as a function of the weighting given to each factor. Various approaches have
been adopted to prepare such landslide susceptibility maps and can be broadly categorized
into two main approaches i.e., the direct or qualitative method and the indirect or  quantitative
method. The direct methods are knowledge -driven driven depend on heuristic approaches. In
the knowledge -driven model, the complicated non -linear relationship between landslide
susceptibility and landslide -causing factors is extracted by assig ning weight to the factors
based on expert knowledge. The success of the knowledge -driven model is mainly based on
expert knowledge (van Westen et al., 2003). The indirect or quantitative methods used by
many researchers are the Analytical Hierarchy Proces s (AHP), Artificial Neural Network
(ANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neuro -Fuzzy and bivariate statistical methods such
as Statistical Index (SI), Frequency ratio (FR), Certainty factor (CF).
Guidelines for Meso-scale landslide susceptibility mapping (GSI 2020) were followed
for the present study and susceptibility zonation. The deliverables of the proposed study are a
1:10000 scale Landslide susceptibility map and a detailed landslide inventory database. The
map categorises the hill slopes in terms of their susceptibility to slope failure based on
processes and the inventory database will provide detailed attributes in terms of material and
movement type/failure mechanism. The outcome of the study provides the basic inputs to
stakeholders for regional e mergency planning allocates resources for risk mitigation and
enhances community preparedness. The Meso -scale study is taken up so that the output is
used by stakeholders in developmental planning at the local scale. Hence, in addition to the
landslide susceptibility map, a user-friendly theme-based qualitative Landslide mitigation and
management map depicting i) locations of trouble spots or areas of varied stability scenarios,
ii) safe locations/ routes, iii) locations of unstable slopes with specific rem edial/ mitigative

damage to the area, including the destruction of several buildings, roads, and other

Out of 48 landslides, all are failures resulting from slope cut, which includes 34 nos.

exposed. During the monsoon time, due to incessant rainfall, there is development of positive
pore pressures in soil profiles due to the infiltration of water runoff from higher reaches of the
slope which triggers the saturated slope material to fail. Development of rills and gullies or
widening of existing stream channels due to erosion was also observed.

LSM at macro scale (1:50,000) helps infrastructure development projects in fragile
mountainous terrains for which standard methodologies are in practice (BIS, 1998). A
landslide susceptibility map on a meso scale (1:10,000/1 : 5,000) can be used for detailed
project planning of any land use development schemes well in advance. Landslide analysis at
this scale helps to narrow down geo -environmentally suitable/feasible sites with respect to
ground instability. For the area of in terest, the methodology provided by GSI in Standard
Operating Procedure (SOP) for Mesoscale (1: 10,000/1:5000) Landslide Susceptibility
Mapping (MLSM) (GSI, 2020) is adopted, which is shown as a flow diagram in (Figure. 5.1).
This method involves the prepa ration of various thematic maps, field validation of various
thematic layers, collection of soil and rock samples, assigning numerals ratings and weighing
of relevant geo -factor maps based on failure domain, blending of data in GIS environment
and classifying and validating the landslide susceptibility map.
It is to keep in consideration that this study is based on the geo -environmental
conditions that existed at the particular time of the study period and does not include the
changes that can be introduced  in the future by natural processes, rainfall or anthropogenic
activities. So, the susceptibility zones can vary then what has been predicted by this study
under a changed scenario. The meso scale landslide study activity includes three phases
namely- pre-field studies, field studies and data augmentation and post-field studies.
During landslide susceptibility modelling of the study area, rated and weighted maps
per failure domain are integrated in a GIS platform using the Weighted Multi -class Index
Overlay method and prepared domain -specified susceptibility maps and were finally
combined as a Combined Landslide Susceptibility Map (Fig. 5.5)  following the steps
mentioned in the approved SOP (Methodology). The landslide susceptibility map is prepared
of the r espective domains namely, Cut -slope, Rockslide and Debris slide domain
respectively. The modelling was not carried out for the No -slide domain. Consequently, all
these domains were clubbed together to generate the combined landslide susceptibility map

Tirumala Hill, located in Tirupati town, Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, is a popular
pilgrimage destination that attracts millions of visitors every year. While the area is known
for its stunning natural beauty and rich cultural heritage, it is also subje ct to several
geological hazards, including landslides. In recent years, slope failures along cut -slopes have
become more frequent in Tirumala hills owing to infrastructure development in the terrain
and construction of roads without adopting adequate supp orting measures for the excavated
hill slopes. This high level of human activity (residential and commercial developments) can
further increase the risk of landslides, as it can destabilize the slopes and alter the natural
drainage patterns. Hence a mesosc ale (1:10,000) landslide susceptibility mapping program in
and around Tirumala Hills, has been carried out in FS: 2022 -23. The study area lies in the
Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh and falls in SOI Toposheet no. 57O/6(13°41'30.22"N
79°20'14.65"E and 13°38'23.06"N, 79°25'24.21"E). The main objective of this field item is to
prepare domain-specific landslide susceptibility models as well as a combined & classified
landslide susceptibility map on a 10K scale for the benefit of stakeholders.
Physiographically, the area under study is characterized by highly dissected ridges
and valleys.  Cuddapah Quartzites forming the cap rock are very intensely dissected and
gullied and the slope of Tirumala hills is constituted by the granites, granitic gneisses
belonging to PGC with basic intrusive. These slopes are dominantly overcast by the slope
wash and debris materials brought down from overlying Cuddapah Quartzite.
The study area is a part of granitic/gneiss terrain and lies at the southern tip of the
Cuddapah b asin. The study area exposes the rocks of the Dharwar Supergroup of the
Archaean age and Peninsular Gneissic Complex -II of the Paleoproterozoic age overlain by
litho units of the Nallamalai Group of the Meso -Proterozoic age.  A major part of the study
area exposes the rocks of Peninsular Gneissic Complex -II comprising grey biotite granite,
pink biotite granite, alkali -feldspar granite and leucogranite and traversed by younger quartz
As a part of pre -field work, landslide inventory was  prepared with the help of
multitemporal high-resolution Google Earth imageries aided with media reports about recent
landslides in and around Tirumala hills, and a total of 12 numbers of landslide imprints /scars
During mesos cale susceptibility mapping in and around Tirumala Hills, along
Tirumala up-ghat road and Tirumala down ghat road, a total of 48 landslide incidences were
recorded and landslide inventory was prepared. Out of 48 landslides, all the failures resulting
from slope cuts, include 34 nos. of debris slides, 14 nos. of Rockslides and Rockfall. The
entire stretch of Tirumala up -ghat road and Tirumala down -ghat road was mapped on a
1:10,000 scale to understand the geological disposition and attitude of litho units, j oint
system, joint pattern, and other structural discontinuities if any. The slope forming material
map and overburden thickness map were prepared in the field to understand and classify the
area into rock domain and overburden domain, based on these factors the landslide incidences
are categorised as Rockslide Domain, Cut-slope Domain, and Debris Domain.  The rock mass
characterisation was done for rock domain areas along the Tirumala up -ghat road and
Tirumala down -ghat road and it is observed that the roc k mass along the cut -slopes and
natural slopes of Tirumala Up -ghat road ranges from Fair rock mass category (Class -III) to
Good Rock mass category (Class -II), while the Tirumala down -ghat road is coming under
good rock mass (Class -II) category. The Slope m ass rating (SMR) for the Tirumala up -ghat
road section falls under the class -III category suggesting that the rock mass is normal and
It is inferred that during the process of slope excavations, the natural slope is modified
at a steeper  angle, the natural drainage path is blocked, and the excavated slope face is left
untreated leading to an unfavourable disposition of structural discontinuities. Moreover,
seepages/ water runoff along the weak bedrock interface add to the further degradat ion of
rock mass. Among the natural factors, Slope Forming Material (SFM) has a more
consequential effect towards the vulnerability of slopes to landslides. SFM in the Tirumala
UP-Road is predominantly comprised of 1m to 2m thick colluvium in general at pl aces, the
SFM along the road section is Slope-Wash material having a thickness of less than one meter,
while nearer to the Tirumala Temple area (Plateau area), the SFM is comprised of 1m to 2m
thick immature soil. Along Tirumala Down-Road, the SFM is mostly Slope-Wash material or
at places thickly bedded quartzites -Shale intercalations are exposed. During the monsoon
season, due to incessant rainfall, there is a development of positive pore pressures in soil
profiles due to the infiltration of water runoff from higher reaches of the slope that triggers
the saturated slope material to fail. Development of rills and gullies or widening of existing
stream channels due to erosion was also observed.

with their LSPW and TESV, the landslide susceptibility map was prepared, which classified
the road corridor along Tirumala up -ghat road and down ghat road into low, moderate, and
highly susceptible areas. Low or No slide domain occupies 40.08%, moderate susceptibility
zone 43.59% and high susceptibility zone 12.33% of 36.17 sq. km of total area.

Regolith thickness varies from 0m-2m.  Based on the RMR and SMR the road section falls in
fair to good category and partially stable respectively.
Tirumala up-road from 8km -12km road section classified as moderate susceptibility

that the zone falls in fair to good category and is partially stable.
